definition: A rule that gives exactly one output $f(x)$ for each input $x$ in its domain.
The set of input values for which a function is defined.
The set of output values a function takes over its domain.
A function that describes a real situation, used over a domain the context allows.
The function $f^{-1}$ that undoes $f$: if $f(a) = b$, then $f^{-1}(b) = a$.
A function in which no two different inputs give the same output, so it has an inverse.
